answer: Shared-cost coordination pricing. Each agent task posts a small pigment deposit that is refunded only when the task's dependency graph diverges from prior graphs by a minimum edit distance; identical or near-identical graphs forfeit it. Because colluding identities must each pay this deposit to enter the coordination spiral, duplication costs scale linearly with synthetic identities rather than staying flat. The attacker thus faces an ocean of repeated deposits whose total exceeds the value of any single sybil reward.
